headline: Coach +15% and a beat on Q4, but a cautious FY27 outlook (mid-single-digit growth) sent Tapestry shares sharply lower.
guidance_note: Initiated FY27: revenue $8.4-8.5B (midpoint just below ~$8.47B consensus), non-GAAP EPS $7.80-7.90; H1 high-single-digit growth, H2 mid-single.
key_messages: Revenue +9% reported, +11% pro forma cc; Coach +15% (+14% cc); North America +7%, Europe +19% (pro forma cc).
Handbag AUR up mid-teens with units roughly flat, a deliberate move to fewer promotions.
FY26: ~11M new customers across brands (about 9M Coach), led by Gen Z; FY26 non-GAAP EPS $7.05 (+38%).
Non-GAAP gross margin 78.1% (+180 bps), helped by operations and the Stuart Weitzman exit.
Tariffs seen as a net benefit in H1 FY27 and a headwind in H2, roughly neutral for the year.

consumer.big_ticket: Handbag demand solid at much higher prices; units flat.
consumer.pricing: Strong pricing power: AUR up mid-teens on reduced discounting; tariffs expected to swing from tailwind to headwind during FY27.

macro_read: Shoppers kept paying more for Coach bags, but management's guide for slower FY27 growth signals it expects the pace of aspirational-luxury spending to cool.
notes: Growth excludes Stuart Weitzman (sold) and is in constant currency. It is revenue growth, not a like-for-like comp.
GAAP EPS $1.68 exceeded non-GAAP $1.32: certain items added $0.36 per share (a gain); non-GAAP excludes them.
Stock fell sharply on report day, but sources disagree on the size (premarket -8.9%, intraday -14%, -16% cited); no confirmed close, so null.
Revenue growth 9% reported; pro forma growth excludes Stuart Weitzman, sold in 2025.
One transcript summary cited Q4 North America +10%; the release says +7%, used here.
